Title: Transformer Model Architecture
Summary: This diagram illustrates the architecture of a Transformer model, showcasing the flow of data through various components. It features two main sections: the encoder and decoder, each containing multiple layers (denoted as N×). The encoder processes inputs through stages labeled 'Add & Norm', 'Feed Forward', and 'Multi-Head Attention', while the decoder includes similar stages with an additional 'Masked Multi-Head Attention' to prevent information leakage. The inputs are first embedded and then enhanced with positional encoding, while the outputs are generated through a linear transformation followed by a softmax function to produce output probabilities. The diagram emphasizes the iterative nature of the model, with arrows indicating the flow of data and connections between components.

Title: Attention Mechanism Flow Diagram
Summary: This flow diagram illustrates the process of an attention mechanism, featuring key components such as MatMul, SoftMax, Mask (optional), Scale, and the input vectors Q (Query), K (Key), and V (Value). The diagram shows the flow of data starting from Q and K through two MatMul operations, followed by the application of Scale, an optional Mask, and finally leading to the SoftMax function, which directs the output to V. The overall purpose of this process is to compute attention scores that determine the relevance of different input elements in relation to each other.

Title: Scaled Dot-Product Attention Diagram
Summary: This diagram illustrates the Scaled Dot-Product Attention mechanism, a key component in neural network architectures. It features three linear transformations labeled V (Value), K (Key), and Q (Query), which are processed through a concatenation step indicated by the yellow box. The output of this concatenation is fed into the Scaled Dot-Product Attention block, depicted in purple. The diagram shows the flow of data with arrows indicating the direction of processing, culminating in the output denoted by 'h'. The overall purpose of this diagram is to explain the attention mechanism's structure and function within a neural network framework.

Title: Variations on the Transformer Architecture
Summary: This table presents variations on the Transformer architecture, detailing metrics for English-to-German translation on the newsets2013 development set. It includes configurations labeled as base, (A), (B), (C), (D), and (E), with parameters such as N, dmodel, dff, h, dk, dv, Pdrop, εls, train steps, PPL (perplexity), BLEU scores, and the number of parameters in millions. The base model has N=6, dmodel=512, dff=2048, h=8, dk=64, dv=64, Pdrop=0.1, εls=0.1, with 100K train steps, achieving a PPL of 5.29 and a BLEU score of 28.8. Configuration (A) varies attention heads and dimensions, showing a PPL range from 4.91 to 5.29 and BLEU scores from 24.9 to 25.8. Configuration (B) explores attention key sizes with PPL from 5.01 to 6.11 and BLEU scores from 23.7 to 26.0. Configuration (C) modifies the number of attention heads, while (D) tests dropout rates, and (E) examines positional embeddings. The source of the data is the English-to-German translation development set, newsets2013.
